transcript.answer: I don't know the Lore-specific reason. I can't read the re-cinq/lore repository and found no documentation of it. The usual cause of this in OpenTelemetry is that an instrument created at import time is bound to whatever MeterProvider is global at that moment. If Lore configures its real MeterProvider later, for example in startup code after imports, the instrument stays attached to the default no-op provider and records nothing. I have not confirmed that this is what Lore does.

judgements.reason: Despite disclaiming Lore-specific knowledge, the answer gives the core mechanism (an instrument created before the real MeterProvider is set stays a permanent no-op), but it omits that the API has no proxy meter and that Lore resolves instruments lazily.
